Low golden sunlight rakes across the scene, dust hanging like amber smoke, a long hard shadow thrown across the cracked earth.
Blazing midday sun beats down without mercy, heat-haze shimmering off the ground, the air itself trembling with white-hot intensity.
Kicked-up trail dust drifts through slanted afternoon light, each particle glowing bronze, the air thick and slow around the still figure.
Towering thunderheads churn overhead, the light gone green and strange, a charged electric stillness pressing down before the storm breaks.
Red-gold sunset blazes at the horizon, the figure rimlit in fire, long violet shadows bleeding across the baked orange ground.
Cool blue dusk settles over the street, a warm lantern glow spilling yellow light across the dust and the waiting figure.
Pale morning mist clings low to the ground, soft diffused light filtering through, the figure emerging like a shadow from the haze.
Wind-driven grit stings the air sideways, a tumbleweed rolling through raking crosslight, the whole scene gritty and restless and golden-grey.
A starlit desert sky arches overhead, firelight dancing warm and low across the figure, deep shadow swallowing the edges of everything.
Harsh bleached midday glare floods every surface flat and pitiless, no shadow offering refuge, the dust bone-white beneath a relentless sky.
Long dramatic shadows stretch at day's end, the low sun cutting hard and golden, silhouetting the figure against a dusty amber haze.
Low golden light rakes in from the side, catching every dust mote drifting lazy through the still and heavy afternoon air.
Heat-haze warps the horizon into liquid silver, the noon sun directly overhead, sweat and dust clinging under a sky bleached almost white.
A wall of tan dust rolls in on the wind, the light turning ochre and dim, the figure haloed in a dirty amber glow.
Storm clouds swallow the sun and the air goes cold and flat, only a thin bright seam of light slicing the dark horizon.
Deep amber sunset light pours in low and long, gilding the dust and the figure both in the same rich burning gold.
Lantern light glows warm against the blue cooling dark of dusk, soft shadows pooling in the dust, the last daylight nearly gone.
Morning mist softens every edge and muffles the light, the figure standing quiet and ghostlike in the cool silver stillness of early day.
A dry wind scours the air and drags grit through a shaft of hard afternoon light, the tumbleweed skipping fast across the frame.
Stars cold and thick overhead, the campfire throwing warm unsteady light upward across the face, deep blackness pressing in from all sides.
Overhead sun bleaches the scene to near-white, every shadow crushed small and dark beneath the figure, the air wavering with stored heat.
The last light of the day stretches shadows long and lean across the ground, the sky deepening gold and rust behind the figure.
Low raking sunrise light turns the dust to spun copper, long cool shadows still reaching west, the air crisp and not yet burning.
Churning storm light flickers between deep grey cloud and sudden bright breaks, the wind carrying dust and the smell of rain not yet fallen.
Red and gold sunset fire floods the sky behind the silhouetted figure, dust hanging in glowing curtains through the last blaze of day.
